# Requirements Document — visual-design

## Introduction

This spec resolves the visual identity that the `design-system.md` steering document deliberately
deferred, and applies it across the already-built site. The chosen direction is **minimal + one
accent**: keep the current clean, near-neutral foundation and introduce a single restrained brand
accent for interactive emphasis. This spec decides the identity (within the design system's fixed
rules and gates — it does not change those), then migrates `src/styles/tokens.css`, the per-section
styles, and the eight `(site)` sections to it, and lands the CI/code hardening the design-system
gates depend on. The `(playground)` route group is out of scope (style-isolated; it owns its own
presentation).

Concrete values (the exact accent hue/OKLCH values, the precise type-scale numbers and spacing
steps) are determined in the Design phase; this document fixes *what* must be true.

## Alignment with Product Vision

This realizes the visual system that `product.md` points to in `design-system.md`. It serves the
**professional inbound funnel** (a coherent, credible presence for recruiters), the **"approachable
and human"** and **"wide and spacious"** principles, and the **responsive** and **accessible**
mandates — while staying inside the design system's accessibility and performance gates and
`product.md`'s "no unnecessary JavaScript on content pages." It replaces the placeholder-neutral
starting look with a deliberate identity without a heavyweight rebrand.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — Coherent identity across the site

**User Story:** As a recruiter visiting the site, I want every page to feel like one deliberate,
professional product, so that it reads as credible builder-evidence rather than a template.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any `(site)` route is viewed THEN it SHALL render with the single shared, token-driven
   identity defined by this spec, in both light and dark themes.
2. WHEN the redesigned site is compared against the `design-baseline/` screenshots THEN every
   `(site)` section SHALL visibly reflect the applied identity, not the placeholder-neutral baseline.
3. The identity SHALL be expressed entirely through design-system token roles; no page or component
   SHALL introduce one-off colors, font sizes, or spacing values.

### Requirement 2 — Minimal base with a single brand accent

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want a clean near-neutral base with one restrained accent, so that the
site has identity without looking busy or amateur.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The base palette SHALL remain near-neutral; a SINGLE brand accent SHALL be introduced as a
   design-system role (defined in `tokens.css`, mapped in `@theme`).
2. WHEN the accent is used THEN it SHALL be limited to interactive emphasis — links, primary
   calls-to-action, the focus `ring`, and active/selected states — and SHALL NOT be used as a large
   background surface.
3. IF a UI need can be met by an existing neutral role THEN the accent SHALL NOT be used (restraint
   by default).
4. The accent SHALL be defined for BOTH themes as a matched pair, each value chosen deliberately
   (not auto-derived from the other).

### Requirement 3 — Every color pairing meets AA in both themes

**User Story:** As a visitor on assistive tech or a bright screen, I want sufficient contrast
everywhere, so that the site is legible and accessible.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any text or icon sits on a surface THEN it SHALL meet the design-system contrast gate
   against THAT surface (≥4.5:1 normal text, ≥3:1 large text), in both themes.
2. WHEN the accent is used for text, a stateful control boundary, or the focus ring THEN it SHALL
   meet the applicable bar (text contrast, or non-text ≥3:1 per WCAG 1.4.11).
3. The spec SHALL produce the legal foreground×surface pairing for every pairing the built sections
   actually use (the matrix the design system deferred), verified in both themes.
4. WHEN color conveys state THEN that state SHALL ALSO be conveyed by a non-color signal (WCAG 1.4.1).

### Requirement 4 — Finalized type scale and spacing rhythm

**User Story:** As Matthew maintaining the site, I want a fixed type scale and spacing rhythm, so
that new content stays visually consistent without per-page decisions.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The spec SHALL fix the design-system type scale (steps, ratio, line-heights) and the spacing
   rhythm (which named Tailwind steps express section rhythm and page gutters).
2. WHEN long-form prose is rendered THEN it SHALL hold the ~75-character measure on wide viewports
   and adapt (shrink) on narrow viewports; the professional-profile layout SHALL widen gutters, not
   the prose measure.
3. Components SHALL use named scale and spacing steps only; arbitrary values SHALL fail review.

### Requirement 5 — Status feedback roles defined

**User Story:** As a visitor submitting the contact form, I want clear success/error feedback, so
that I know whether my message sent.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The spec SHALL define `success`, `warning`, and `info` token values (in addition to the existing
   `destructive`) in `tokens.css` and map them in `@theme`, in both themes.
2. WHEN a feedback state is shown THEN it SHALL use a status role (never a one-off color) and SHALL
   pair color with text/icon (not color alone).
3. WHEN the design system lists a role as "active" THEN that role SHALL exist in `tokens.css` and be
   mapped in `@theme` (no doc↔token divergence).

### Requirement 6 — Surfaces and motion decided, restrained

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want a calm, fast interface, so that the site feels polished without
distracting motion or heavy effects.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The spec SHALL decide the surface separation language (retain flat/bordered, or introduce a small
   tokenized elevation set) and apply it consistently.
2. Motion SHALL be minimal and purposeful; `prefers-reduced-motion` SHALL be honored, and any motion
   SHALL stay within the performance gate.
3. WHEN the theme is toggled THEN the UI SHALL NOT flash (no-FOUC), via the documented theming
   mechanism.

### Requirement 7 — Applied across all eight built sections

**User Story:** As a recruiter browsing several pages, I want consistency across the whole site, so
that the experience holds up beyond the landing page.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the identity is finalized THEN it SHALL be applied to all eight `(site)` sections (landing,
   professional profile, projects, contributions, blog, resources, slash pages).
2. FOR EACH built section THEN the spec SHALL decide whether to codify its existing look or re-style
   it to the new identity, and record that decision.
3. The `(playground)` route group SHALL be left unchanged (out of scope).
4. WHEN the work is complete THEN the existing unit and E2E test suites SHALL remain green (no
   functional regressions).

### Requirement 8 — Design-system gates enforced in CI

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want the design-system gates actually enforced, so that future changes
can't silently regress contrast, performance, or doc↔token consistency.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The spec SHALL add an automated check that every role the design system calls "active" exists in
   `tokens.css` and is mapped in `@theme`, failing CI on divergence.
2. The spec SHALL add the deferred Lighthouse assertions — LCP / CLS / INP and a byte-weight budget —
   and extend audited route coverage toward all `(site)` routes (owned by `tech.md`/CI).
3. The spec SHALL set the theming no-flash mechanism (`disableTransitionOnChange`) in code.
4. These CI/code changes SHALL NOT block content authoring (they gate visual/CI regressions, not
   markdown edits).

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity
- **Token-driven**: the identity lives entirely in `src/styles/tokens.css` + the `@theme` mapping and
  per-section CSS; components consume tokens. Adding future content or sections SHALL require no new
  one-off styling.
- **No new runtime dependencies** for the base identity (accent, type, spacing are CSS/token-level).
- **Scoped per-section styles** remain in `src/styles/`; shared component styling stays in the owned
  shadcn primitives.

### Performance
- Static `(site)` pages hold a 90+ Lighthouse Performance score; LCP/CLS/INP within budget; webfont
  CLS bounded. No identity choice may add unnecessary client JS to content pages.

### Accessibility
- The full design-system accessibility contract holds in both themes (AA text contrast, non-text
  1.4.11, visible focus, keyboard, reduced-motion, forced-colors usable, correct image/icon a11y).
  axe passes; keyboard/reduced-motion/forced-colors verified by manual review.

### Reliability
- No regression to existing functionality; existing Vitest and Playwright suites remain green. The
  playground remains visually unaffected.

### Usability
- Correct and legible at all named Tailwind breakpoints (mobile first-class) and in both themes; the
  ~75-character prose measure is respected.
